name: Tinted amber glass slab desk
objectClass: desk / writing table (glass slab construction); class range 1.00–1.80 m wide, 0.55–0.80 m deep, 0.70–0.78 m high

reasons: Single three-quarter view: the rear long side, the underside of the top, the outer face of the far (+X) end panel and the floor contact of both panels are not shown.
Object is a manufactured, left-right symmetric slab assembly, so the hidden end panel and its bracket pair can be mirrored from the visible near end.

Material is transparent tinted glass: the photographed colour is the sum of two overlapping glass thicknesses in places, so per-zone albedo must be approximated and the transmission/thickness tint reconstructed procedurally.
Bracket geometry is small in frame (≈0.10 m arms) and partly read through glass; screw positions are legible but fine profile must be approximated.
Silhouette (two vertical plates plus one horizontal plate) is unambiguous and fills ≈80% of the frame width.

notes: Silhouette: three plate primitives. Top slab ≈1.40 m × 0.70 m × 0.012 m lying horizontal at ≈0.74 m; two vertical end panels each ≈0.64 m (along depth) × ≈0.73 m tall × 0.012 m thick, standing in the X-normal orientation at the ends. Footprint is two parallel lines, not a solid rectangle.
Proportions against the 1.40 m width reference: height 0.53×, depth 0.50×, end-panel depth 0.46×, end-panel height 0.52×, plate thickness 0.009×.

Macro parts (3): top slab; near (−X) end panel; far (+X) end panel. Meso parts: four L-brackets, polished edge bands, the two panel-to-top butt joints. Micro: screw pairs on each bracket arm, two maker decals, bottom-edge contact chamfers.

Spatial relationships: each end panel's top edge butts flush against the underside of the top slab (edge-to-face butt joint, adhesive or gasket not visible). Each L-bracket has its horizontal arm bolted to the underside of the top slab and its vertical arm bolted to the inner face of the end panel, so the bracket wraps the inside of the corner and carries the joint. Panels are set inboard ≈0.03 m from the top's front edge and ends, so the top overhangs on all four sides. Panel bottom edges rest directly on the floor plane.

INFERENCE: the low-roughness, highlight-free faces with visible internal darkening toward thickness suggest body-tinted transparent glass rather than lacquered panel — read as glass with transmission, not as an opaque orange solid.

INFERENCE: brackets are counted as four (two per end panel); only the near pair and two dark forms on the far panel are legible, but a symmetric four-bracket layout is the standard for this construction.
HIDDEN: rear long side of the top slab and the rear vertical edges of both panels; assumed mirror of the front.
HIDDEN: underside of the top slab, including bracket horizontal arms and any adhesive pads.
